text:
sara: quick q — during Llama2-13B q8 bring-up we saw flashattn_v3 beat v2 on us-west H100s but *regress* in eu-west H100s. attaching perf charts, anyone seen region-specific kernel perf like this?

chloe: do we have seq length distribution? flashv3 tends to shine on longer sequences, v2 sometimes wins on short ones.

sara: median seq 512, p95 1024 in us-west; eu-west median 256, p95 768. per-token median latency measurements: us-west H100 flashv3 8.3ms vs v2 9.1ms; eu-west H100 flashv3 11.4ms vs v2 9.8ms — pretty surprising.

ankit: could be driver / CUDA / Triton differences or even host kernel flags. what are the exact versions on eu-west?

sara: eu-west nodes are CUDA 12.1, driver 535.54, Triton 2.20; us-west nodes are CUDA 12.2, driver 536.XX, Triton 2.21. we pin docker images but infra updated host drivers last month.

matt: that rings a bell — flashv3 uses some new fused kernels that are sensitive to driver/runtime combo and memalign. also check cuMemPool fragmentation and NUMA. can you paste microbench logs?

sara: here's a short snippet from the perf probe run:

```
[attn_kernels] batch=8, seqlen=512
flash_attn_v3_fwd: 3.2ms | flash_attn_v2_fwd: 3.9ms
tokens/sec=12.1k | peak_mem=6.8GB
```

chloe: are we building the same quantization artifact? q8 kernels can vary by build (xformers vs nvq8 wrappers). if eu-west got a different q8 package we'd see this.

sara: good catch — us-west uses q8-fast artifact, eu-west ended up with nvq8 due to an older build node. I'm re-running a deploy with identical artifact now.

ankit: operationally, policy suggestion: if flashv3 is slower in a region, fallback that region to Triton kernels or flashv2 until host drivers are aligned. Triton path is more conservative but stable across driver versions.

eva: we should add an automated per-region kernel selection policy in router: prefer flashv3 on H100 when driver >= 536 and Triton/v2 otherwise. also add a perf-probe that runs a microbenchmark at rollout scope.

sara: agree. also need capacity sizing delta: on our bench, Triton path gives ~15% lower throughput vs flashv3 for this model, so eu-west pool needs ~+20% capacity if we keep Triton fallback.

matt: add a dynamic fallback on latency SLOs: if 5m avg latency > target, route new requests to a quantized variant or alternate kernel. also ensure canary rollout runs perf-probe to validate.

deploy-bot: perf-probe job pb-9876 started on cluster eu-west-1 (node group: inference-h100-3).

chloe: FYI flashv3 also usually reduces KV cache memory for large context, which can increase concurrency headroom. document that tradeoff in the kernel matrix.

sara: thanks — I'll post the updated charts + PR with router changes and the per-region kernel policy once the probe finishes.

matt: when you post charts, include the raw microbench commands and environment (CUDA, driver, Triton). that speeds root-cause. :+1:

sara:will do, thx everyone.
